title: [SEC6] Good: SPA fallback handler with extension-based routing
description:
In crates/kithd/src/static_files.rs, the static_handler() (lines 11-33) implements a smart SPA fallback:

- If the path has no extension (no '.'), treat it as a client-side route and serve index.html
- If the path has an extension (e.g., '.js', '.css', '.html'), try to serve it as a file
- 404 only if the file truly doesn't exist and it's not an extensionless path

This allows the browser's JavaScript router to handle paths like /chats/abc without 404ing. The heuristic 'no extension = SPA route' is simple and correct for this use case.

Alternative (always 404 missing files) breaks client-side routing. Alternative (always serve index.html) breaks static asset loading.

Bonus: Use of rust_embed compiles static assets into the binary—no separate file deployment needed. Phase 1 requirement: single musl binary.
